chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥassin ibn Aḥmad, from one whom he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: May I perform salat (prayer) in a black cap? He said, “Do not perform salat (prayer) in it, for it is the clothing of the people of the Fire.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: And salat (prayer) is not valid in a thin garment that reveals due to its thinness, unless there is beneath it something like a waist-wrapper, trousers, or another shirt that is not transparent.

key_terms.أَهْلِ النَّارِ: the people of the Fire, i.e., the inhabitants of Hell
key_terms.السَّوْدَاءِ: black; describing the cap mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْقَلَنْسُوَةِ: a cap or head-cover worn on the head
key_terms.يَشِفُّ: shows through; reveals what is beneath because of transparency

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about praying in black clothing or thin transparent garments?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings concerning clothing in salat (prayer), specifically discouraging prayer in a black cap and prohibiting prayer in a garment so thin that it reveals what is beneath. It highlights the juristic requirement that clothing worn in prayer must provide proper coverage and not be transparent.
